first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and the inherited evidence indicates that shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction can improve early adoption. I would verify these directly relevant records before testing a guarded simplification, while monitoring qualified revenue and downstream retention so an activation lift does not mask lower-quality accounts. Promotional pricing may address competitor pressure but risks margin and sustainable revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, measured test of the shortened onboarding flow, prioritizing the current 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline. The verified record shows a 13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention, making this the strongest evidence for sustainable qualified revenue. Treat signup-field reduction as SMB-only and avoid broad rollout because its 1% retention decline and limited segment evidence create downstream risk. Gate success on qualified revenue, 30-day retention, and activation—not completion alone.

final2.rationale: The deeper competitor cut and doubling churn conversations make price-sensitive SMB defense the immediate priority. Run a tightly targeted, time-limited promotional pricing test for eligible SMB accounts rather than broad discounting. Monitor qualified revenue, gross margin, retention, expansion, and post-promotion churn; stop if the offer mainly subsidizes accounts that would have stayed or attracts lower-quality revenue. The pricing evidence is inherited but unverified this cycle, so keep the test guarded.
